name: Pim-1 proto-oncogene, serine/threonine kinase

function.text: PIM1 encodes serine/threonine-protein kinase pim-1. Annotated molecular activities include protein serine kinase activity and protein serine/threonine kinase activity. It participates in positive regulation of DNA-templated transcription and protein stabilization.

germline.text: No constitutional disease assertion was retrieved in the reviewed GenCC snapshot; this does not exclude a germline association.

somatic.text: Reported somatic alteration contexts include Large B-cell lymphoma of immune-privileged sites. The alteration class and exact variant must be assessed in the disease context.

function.text: PIM1 encodes serine/threonine-protein kinase pim-1. Based in part on similarity, it mediates survival signaling through phosphorylation of BAD, which induces release of the anti-apoptotic protein Bcl-X(L)/BCL2L1. It stimulates cell cycle progression at the G1-S and G2-M transitions by phosphorylation of CDC25A and CDC25C. It promotes cell cycle progression and tumorigenesis by down-regulating expression of a regulator of cell cycle progression, CDKN1B, at both transcriptional and post-translational levels.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving PIM1 have been reported in large b-cell lymphoma of immune-privileged sites, plasma cell myeloma, and non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
